label: SpecInterface
name: StartOptions
signature: interface StartOptions { port: number; hostname: string; keyHex?: string; didWebServicesStr?: string; publicHostname?: string; crawlersStr?: string; log?: Logger }

label: SpecRequirement
text: createFromEnv must import a Secp256k1 keypair from opts.keyHex when it is set, and otherwise create a fresh keypair and emit a warn-level log entry carrying the generated DID before continuing.

label: SpecRequirement
text: createFromEnv must derive the crawlers value from opts.crawlersStr by splitting on commas, trimming each entry, dropping empty entries and de-duplicating the remainder, and must pass undefined when the option is absent.

label: SpecInterface
name: CreateFromEnvOptions
signature: interface CreateFromEnvOptions { keyHex?: string; didWebServicesStr?: string; publicHostname?: string; crawlersStr?: string; log?: Logger }

label: SpecRequirement
text: StartOptions must carry the required port and hostname for the HTTP bind plus the optional keyHex, didWebServicesStr, publicHostname, crawlersStr and log fields, and must be accepted directly as the CreateFromEnvOptions argument to createFromEnv.

label: SpecRequirement
text: createFromEnv must JSON-parse opts.didWebServicesStr into the didWebServices array when the string is present, and on a parse failure must log a warn that the JSON was ignored and leave the array empty rather than throwing.

label: SpecRequirement
text: start must create the repo through createFromEnv with the StartOptions, serve repo.app.fetch with Deno.serve bound to options.port and options.hostname, log an info entry with the port in the onListen callback, and return a StartResult carrying app, server, repo and port.

label: SpecInterface
name: StartResult
signature: interface StartResult { app: RepoFactory["app"]; server: Deno.HttpServer; repo: RepoFactory; port: number }

label: SpecRequirement
text: createFromEnv must build the RepoFactory via createRepoFactory with Deno KV storage, the signer produced from the keypair, publicKeyDid set to the signer DID, publicHostname from opts, the normalised crawlers, didWebServices only when the parsed list is non-empty, and an enabled OAuth server whose issuer is http://127.0.0.1:2583.

label: SpecRequirement
text: createFromEnv and start must use opts.log when supplied and otherwise fall back to the module-level defaultLog, so logging is never undefined at the call sites.

label: SpecRequirement
text: DpopNonceStore issues a nonce for an origin and verifies a supplied nonce against that origin, resolving the verification to a boolean so callers can reject replayed or foreign-origin proofs.

label: SpecInterface
name: IssueTokenResult
signature: interface IssueTokenResult { accessToken: string; refreshToken: string; expiresIn: number }

label: SpecRequirement
text: TokenStore.refresh takes a refresh token and resolves to a fresh IssueTokenResult, or to null when the refresh token is unknown or unusable.

label: SpecInterface
name: DpopProofValidation
signature: interface DpopProofValidation { jkt: string; jti: string }

label: SpecRequirement
text: IssueTokenParams carries the user DID, handle, an optional scope, and a required jkt — the SHA-256 thumbprint of the client DPoP public key — so an issued token is bound to one specific client DPoP key.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TokenStore.validate takes an access token and resolves either to a TokenValidation exposing sub, optional handle, scope, and jkt, or to null when the token is not valid, rather than throwing.

label: SpecRequirement
text: InjectedSession holds the session data typed as OAuthSessionData alongside the DPoP CryptoKeyPair, so the caller can both persist the session and sign subsequent DPoP proofs with the same key.

label: SpecInterface
name: DpopVerifier
signature: interface DpopVerifier { verifyProof(proof: string, method: string, url: string, accessToken?: string): Promise<DpopProofValidation | null> }

label: SpecRequirement
text: TokenStore.issue accepts IssueTokenParams and resolves to an IssueTokenResult containing the access token, refresh token, and expiry in seconds.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TokenStore.revoke takes a token and resolves to void, invalidating it without reporting a result.

label: SpecInterface
name: SessionInjector
signature: interface SessionInjector { injectSession(opts: { userDid: string; handle: string; scope?: string }): Promise<InjectedSession> }

label: SpecRequirement
text: The module declares only pure interfaces and must import no I/O or runtime primitives — no fetch, no crypto, no timers, no Deno.* — so any implementation package can satisfy the contracts.

label: SpecInterface
name: TokenValidation
signature: interface TokenValidation { sub: string; handle?: string; scope: string; jkt: string }

label: SpecRequirement
text: DpopVerifier.verifyProof takes the serialized proof, the HTTP method, the request URL, and an optional access token, and resolves to a DpopProofValidation stating the jkt and jti, or to null when the proof does not verify.

label: SpecInterface
name: TokenStore
signature: interface TokenStore { issue(params: IssueTokenParams): Promise<IssueTokenResult>; validate(accessToken: string): Promise<TokenValidation | null>; refresh(refreshToken: string): Promise<IssueTokenResult | null>; revoke(token: string): Promise<void> }

label: SpecRequirement
text: SessionInjector.injectSession takes a user DID, handle, and optional scope, and resolves to an InjectedSession pairing the OAuthSessionData with the CryptoKeyPair used for DPoP.

label: SpecInterface
name: InjectedSession
signature: interface InjectedSession { sessionData: OAuthSessionData; dpopKeyPair: CryptoKeyPair }

label: SpecInterface
name: IssueTokenParams
signature: interface IssueTokenParams { userDid: string; handle: string; scope?: string; jkt: string }

label: SpecInterface
name: DpopNonceStore
signature: interface DpopNonceStore { issue(origin: string): Promise<string>; verify(origin: string, nonce: string): Promise<boolean> }

label: SpecRequirement
text: Mst.root returns the current root Cid, or null when the tree is empty, and Mst.size returns the number of key entries held.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The MST implementation depends only on the abstract BlockStore and Hasher contracts and performs no I/O beyond them, keeping this layer free of any concrete database or HTTP transport.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Mst.init loads the tree from its BlockStore before use, so subsequent reads and writes operate on nodes that have already been fetched.

label: SpecInterface
name: Signer
signature: interface Signer { did(): Did; sign(bytes: Bytes): Promise<Bytes> }

label: SpecRequirement
text: CommitOp, CommitEvent, SequencedFrame, Sequencer and WriteOp describe the repo write path — an operation, the commit event it produces, the frame the sequencer emits, and the operation requested by a client — and RepoApi is the surface a transport exposes for those writes.

label: SpecInterface
name: createMst
signature: createMst(store: BlockStore, sha256Fn: Hasher, root?: Cid | null): Mst

label: SpecInterface
name: RepoStore
signature: interface RepoStore { getHead(did: Did): Promise<{ commit: Cid; rev: Tid } | null>; setHead(did: Did, head: { commit: Cid; rev: Tid }): Promise<void> }

label: SpecRequirement
text: Mst stores a key to Cid map as an immutable tree of blocks inside a BlockStore, hashing nodes through an injected Hasher, and is constructed from a store, a hasher and a nullable root Cid so an existing tree can be reopened from its root.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Mst.entries walks the tree lazily as an AsyncIterable of key/value pairs, so a large tree is enumerated without materializing every entry at once.

label: SpecRequirement
text: mod.ts is the package's single public entrypoint and re-exports both the contract types from contracts.ts and the MST implementation from mst.ts, so consumers import the package once.

label: SpecRequirement
text: XrpcError carries an XrpcErrorName and a message, and its toJSON produces exactly { error, message } so handlers can serialize it as an AT Protocol XRPC error body.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Mst.get returns the Cid stored for a key or null when the key is absent; Mst.set inserts or replaces the key and returns the new root Cid; Mst.delete removes the key and returns the previous root Cid, or null when the key was not present.

label: SpecInterface
name: XrpcError.constructor
signature: constructor(error: XrpcErrorName, message: string, status?: number)

label: SpecInterface
name: collect
signature: collect(cid: Cid | null, set: Set<Cid>): Promise<void>

label: SpecRequirement
text: diff returns the Cids of blocks reachable from the new root but not from the old root, giving a sync peer exactly the blocks it is missing, and collect walks a tree from a Cid accumulating every reachable Cid into a caller-supplied Set.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The HTTP status is optional when constructing an XrpcError, so an error can be raised before a transport has decided a status code for it.

label: SpecInterface
name: diff
signature: diff(store: BlockStore, oldRoot: Cid | null, newRoot: Cid | null): Promise<Cid[]>

label: SpecInterface
name: Verifier
signature: interface Verifier { verify(did: Did, bytes: Bytes, sig: Bytes): Promise<boolean> }

label: SpecRequirement
text: Did is a plain string alias naming a repository account, and every contract that identifies a repo (signing, verification, head lookup) takes a Did rather than an untyped string.

label: SpecRequirement
text: BlockStore is the content-addressed block boundary keyed by Cid and Storage layers record persistence above it, while RepoStore records each repo's head as a commit Cid paired with a rev Tid, returning null from getHead when a repo has no head yet and overwriting it through setHead.

label: SpecInterface
name: Mst.entries
signature: entries(): AsyncIterable<{ key: string; value: Cid }>

label: SpecRequirement
text: Signer reports its own did and signs a byte string into a signature; Verifier independently checks a signature against a did and the signed bytes and answers with a boolean, so commit signing and verification are separable roles.

label: SpecInterface
name: Mst.constructor
signature: constructor(store: BlockStore, root: Cid | null, sha256Fn: Hasher)

label: SpecRequirement
text: createMst builds an Mst from a BlockStore and a Hasher with an optional root Cid, so callers open a tree through one factory instead of the constructor.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TokenStore.revoke deletes the stored entry identified by the presented token's jti and is a no-op (no error) for a token that cannot be decoded or is unknown.

label: SpecInterface
name: ParRequest
signature: interface ParRequest { clientId: string; codeChallenge: string; codeChallengeMethod: string; redirectUri: string; scope: string; state: string; responseType: string; expiresAt: number }

label: SpecRequirement
text: createDpopVerifier tracks seen jtis with a JTI_TTL_MS of five minutes: isReplayed returns false and purges an entry whose deadline has passed, returns true while it has not, and recordJti stamps the jti with now + JTI_TTL_MS and lazily sweeps expired entries once the map exceeds 1000 entries.

label: SpecRequirement
text: computeCodeChallenge hashes the verifier with SHA-256 and encodes the digest as unhyphenated base64url with padding stripped, implementing the S256 PKCE challenge used by authorization code validation.

label: SpecInterface
name: verifyClientAssertion
signature: verifyClientAssertion(assertion: string, clientId: string, issuer: string): Promise<boolean>

label: SpecInterface
name: verifyProof
signature: verifyProof(proof: string, method: string, url: string, accessToken?: string): Promise<DpopProofValidation | null>

label: SpecInterface
name: ParStore
signature: interface ParStore { store(params: Omit<ParRequest, "expiresAt">): Promise<string>; consume(requestUri: string): Promise<ParRequest | null> }

label: SpecRequirement
text: TokenStore.refresh returns null unless the presented token decodes, is unexpired, and maps to a stored entry of type "refresh" whose re-signed form equals the token; on success it deletes the old jti (revocation), then issues a new access/refresh pair preserving the original userDid, handle, scope and cnf.jkt.

label: SpecInterface
name: makeToken
signature: makeToken(params: IssueTokenParams, type: "access" | "refresh", expiresIn: number): Promise<string>

label: SpecRequirement
text: TokenStore.validate returns null when the access token payload cannot be decoded, when jti is absent or the literal "undefined", when exp has passed, when no stored entry exists for that jti or the stored entry is not of type "access", or when re-signing the stored claims does not reproduce the presented token; otherwise it returns sub, handle, scope defaulted to "atproto" and jkt taken from cnf.jkt.

label: SpecRequirement
text: cleanJwk copies only the kty, crv, x and y members of a JsonWebKey, plus d when it is defined, into a plain string record, so exported key material carries no extra WebCrypto fields.

label: SpecRequirement
text: buildHtu strips query string and fragment from a URL and returns origin concatenated with pathname, so DPoP htu comparisons ignore query and fragment.

label: SpecRequirement
text: createMemoryTokenStore(signer) issues an access token with a 900 second lifetime and a refresh token with a 604800 second lifetime, each signed by the supplied Signer as a JWT with typ at+jwt or refresh+jwt respectively, carrying iss = signer.did(), sub = userDid, handle, scope defaulting to "atproto", cnf.jkt, iat, exp and a fresh random UUID jti; both tokens are retained in an in-memory map keyed by jti and issue() returns { accessToken, refreshToken, expiresIn: 900 }.

label: SpecRequirement
text: createMemoryParStore stores each pushed request under "urn:ietf:params:oauth:request_uri:<uuid>" with a 60000 ms expiry, garbage-collects expired entries on store, and its consume is one-time: it deletes the entry, returns null when it is missing or expired, and otherwise returns the stored ParRequest.

label: SpecInterface
name: NonceEntry
signature: interface NonceEntry { current: string; previous: string | null; previousExpiresAt: number; expiresAt: number }

label: SpecRequirement
text: createMemoryAuthorizationCodeStore stores each created code as an AuthorizationCode with userDid, handle, scope, codeChallenge, codeChallengeMethod, redirectUri and a 300000 ms expiry under a random UUID code; validate deletes the code before any further test (single use), returns null when it is unknown or expired, recomputes the challenge from the presented codeVerifier and returns null on mismatch, otherwise returning userDid, handle and scope.

label: SpecRequirement
text: verifyClientAssertion returns false unless the assertion is a three-part JWT with alg ES256 whose iss equals clientId, whose aud equals issuer, whose exp has not passed, whose iat is no more than 60 seconds in the future, and which carries a jti, and unless client metadata resolvable for clientId yields a JWKS (inline jwks or a jwks_uri fetch returning 200) from which a key matching the header kid, or the first key when no kid is given, verifies the ECDSA P-256 SHA-256 signature over the signing input; any exception yields false.

label: SpecRequirement
text: createDpopNonceStore keeps, per origin, a NonceEntry holding current, previous, previousExpiresAt and expiresAt: issue rotates the existing current into previous with a 30 second grace deadline and stores a fresh random UUID current with a five minute expiry, and verify consumes and deletes the current nonce when it matches and is unexpired, or accepts an unexpired previous nonce within the grace window and consumes it, returning false for unknown or expired nonces.

label: SpecInterface
name: AuthorizationCodeStore
signature: interface AuthorizationCodeStore { create(params): Promise<string>; validate(code: string, codeVerifier: string): Promise<{ userDid: string; handle: string; scope: string } | null> }

label: SpecRequirement
text: createSessionInjector(tokenStore, pdsUrl) generates a fresh P-256 ECDSA keypair for every injectSession call, exports both JWKs, computes the jkt thumbprint from the public JWK, issues DPoP-bound tokens through the token store with scope defaulting to "atproto", and returns sessionData containing accessJwt, refreshJwt, userDid, handle, pds = pdsUrl, and the cleaned public/private DPoP JWKs alongside the live CryptoKeyPair.

label: SpecRequirement
text: fetchClientMetadata serves a successful result from a five minute in-memory cache; on a miss it fetches the client_id URL, and returns null unless the response is HTTP 200 with an application/json content-type and the document has client_id equal to the requested id, a non-empty redirect_uris array, grant_types including "authorization_code", a scope containing "atproto" and dpop_bound_access_tokens true; it returns null on any thrown error and caches only accepted metadata.

label: SpecRequirement
text: verifyProof returns null unless the proof is a three-part JWT whose header has typ "dpop+jwt" and alg "ES256", whose jwk is EC P-256 with string x and y and no private d member, whose htm equals the uppercased request method, whose htu equals buildHtu(url), whose iat is within CLOCK_SKEW_SEC (30s) of now, whose ath (when present alongside an access token) equals the base64url SHA-256 of that token, whose ECDSA P-256 SHA-256 signature verifies against the embedded key, and whose jti is present and not already replayed; on success it records the jti and returns { jkt, jti }.

label: SpecInterface
name: AuthorizationCode
signature: interface AuthorizationCode { code: string; userDid: string; handle: string; scope: string; codeChallenge: string; codeChallengeMethod: string; redirectUri: string; expiresAt: number }

label: SpecInterface
name: ClientMetadata
signature: interface ClientMetadata { client_id: string; redirect_uris: string[]; grant_types: string[]; scope: string; dpop_bound_access_tokens: boolean; jwks?: { keys: Array<Record<string, unknown>> }; jwks_uri?: string }

intent: This context covers the wiring layer that turns process-level options into a running PDS instance in hono-pds: it owns keypair import or generation, Deno KV storage creation, parsing and normalisation of the did-web-services JSON and crawler list, and the createRepoFactory call that assembles the repository factory. It exists so the configuration surface (CreateFromEnvOptions) and the server lifecycle (StartOptions / StartResult, the start helper) can be exercised directly in tests and embedded by other launchers such as the worker-launcher script, without going through a CLI flag parser.
label: SpecContext
name: hono-pds

intent: This context exists to fix the shape of OAuth server state handling without committing to any transport or storage mechanism. By declaring IssueTokenParams, IssueTokenResult, TokenValidation, TokenStore, InjectedSession, SessionInjector, DpopProofValidation, DpopVerifier, and DpopNonceStore as pure interfaces with no imports of fetch, crypto, timers, or Deno APIs, it lets concrete impl packages (such as lib/atproto-oauth-server-deno) be swapped in behind a stable contract. It is the dependency boundary that the rest of the OAuth server code compiles against, and it carries the DPoP binding requirement: tokens are tied to a client key thumbprint (jkt) at issue time and re-checked at validation and proof-verification time.
label: SpecContext
name: lib-abc-atproto-oauth-server

intent: This context exists to fix the interface contract that every concrete AT Protocol repo transport implements against, so storage backends, signers, and XRPC handlers can be swapped without touching repo semantics. It separates the abstract layer (types, MST algorithm) from the Deno/KV/IndexedDB and Hono implementations that live in sibling packages, and it pins the error shape (XrpcError) that handlers serialize onto the wire.
label: SpecContext
name: lib-abc-atproto-repo

intent: This context exists to specify the Deno OAuth server building blocks that hono-pds composes into its PDS: token issuance and validation, session injection, DPoP proof and nonce handling, authorization-code/PKCE, pushed authorization requests, and OAuth client metadata/assertion verification. It is the implementation side of the sc.hono-pds ABC contracts, so the requirements here define the security semantics (binding, expiry, replay, single-use) that any replacement store must preserve.
label: SpecContext
name: lib-atproto-oauth-server-deno
